The must-sees

6 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Fortress · 1890

    Alte Feste

    German colonial troops began it in 1890 as their headquarters. For decades it housed the national history museum.

  2. 02
    Church · 1910

    Christuskirche

    Built from local quartz sandstone and consecrated in 1910, it mixes neo-Romanesque and Art Nouveau. The stained-glass windows were a gift from Kaiser Wilhelm II.

    Look for

    Inside, plaques name German soldiers killed in the colonial wars of 1904–1908. The far greater number of Herero and Nama dead are not named.

  3. 03
    Landmark · 2002

    Heroes’ Acre

    Inaugurated on Heroes’ Day 2002, it honours those who fought colonialism and apartheid. A bronze Unknown Soldier and a tall obelisk look out over the Auas Mountains.

    Look for

    Below the obelisk, rows of tombs honour named heroes, among them anti-colonial leaders such as Hendrik Witbooi and Samuel Maharero.

  4. 04
    Museum · 2014

    Independence Memorial Museum

    Built by a North Korean firm and opened in 2014, it is often likened to a coffee pot. Outside, a statue of Sam Nujoma and a memorial to the 1904–1908 genocide of the Herero and Nama.

  5. 05
    Neighbourhood · 1959

    Katutura

    Black residents were forcibly moved here from the Old Location from 1959. The Otjiherero name means the place where we do not want to live; today it is full of markets, music and street life.

    Look for

    At Single Quarters market, look for kapana: strips of beef grilled over open fires and eaten on the spot with spicy salt.

  6. 06
    Civic building · 1913

    Tintenpalast

    Completed in 1913 as the colonial administration building, it earned its nickname from the amount of ink spent inside. Since 1990 it has housed the National Assembly.

    Look for

    In the gardens in front stand statues of leaders who resisted colonial rule, among them Hendrik Witbooi, the Nama chief who fought the Germans.
